audience.programmeDescription: Radboud Mathematics develops abstract mathematical reasoning and practical modelling. Its ordinary bachelor combines calculus, analysis, linear and abstract algebra, programming and probability with a chosen mathematical line, open study space and an individual mathematics thesis. The comparison uses the Wiskunde line, including topology, rings and fields, differential equations and restricted advanced choices.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers three related directions built around mathematical methods, computation and statistics, with economic or biomedical applications. The economic direction adds economic models, econometrics and financial analysis. The biomedical direction combines mathematical and computational methods with biological measurements, image-processing applications and quantitative pharmacology. Real and complex analysis, abstract algebra, topology, measure theory and partial differential equations remain substantial gaps. General biology and business study provide application context rather than replacing that mathematics.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC comprises 54 EC required first-year courses, 6 EC first-year free choice, 24 EC later common courses, 36 EC in the selected line, 48 EC later free choice and a 12 EC individual thesis. The line includes 18 EC prescribed and 18 EC restricted choices, with at least 6 EC from year three. Optional minors, mobility and combined degrees are not universal requirements. Normal first-year study advice requires 39 EC, subject to applicable exceptions. RADAr language-test participation is required without extra credit; passing is not required. Thesis prior knowledge comprises the compulsory first-two-year courses. Topic approval, registration, two assessors and interim/final presentations with active peer participation apply. The thesis normally runs in spring. The chosen bachelor composition requires board approval at least three months before graduation.

programmeConcepts.label: Mathematics, computation & statistical modelling
programmeConcepts.concept: Combine calculus, linear algebra, probability and numerical methods with algorithms, statistical learning and economic modelling. This computational and applied direction develops mathematical problem-solving while leaving substantial gaps in Radboud’s pure-mathematics sequence and compulsory thesis.

programmeConcepts.label: Mathematics, statistics & economic decisions
programmeConcepts.concept: Apply mathematical and statistical models to economic behaviour, financial decisions and business information, retaining numerical and algebraic foundations. The shared mathematics backbone covers methods, linear algebra, multivariable calculus, numerical equations, signals and probability; it does not reproduce the selected pure-mathematics sequence or its compulsory thesis.

programmeConcepts.label: Mathematics, computation & biomedical modelling
programmeConcepts.concept: Combine calculus, linear algebra, probability, numerical algorithms and statistical learning with biomedical measurements and quantitative pharmacological models. General image-processing methods and biological and anatomical study support medical applications; this applied combination leaves substantial gaps in the pure-mathematics sequence and is not a clinical Medicine curriculum.

notes.text: Radboud’s selected Wiskunde line includes a deeper sequence in real and complex analysis, abstract algebra, topology, measure theory and partial differential equations. These UCR programmes instead combine mathematical methods with computation, statistics and economic or biomedical applications; they do not reproduce that pure-mathematics sequence.

Radboud requires an individual 12 EC mathematics thesis with supervision, interim and final presentations, and active peer participation. Optional UCR independent research is additional, approval-dependent and outside the displayed 180 EC. A UCR composition does not establish degree equivalence, a teaching qualification or admission to a particular master.
